races.name: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
Jack Frost Chiller & Freezer Hire Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's five-year-old has recent placing form over 16-17f on good ground (0W3P sim-going), and wearing headgear on turf; as a genuine hold-up type he may end up closer to the pace by default in this tactical vacuum, which could actually serve him in a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Jim and Suzi Best's six-year-old steps back up to 2m after a 47-day break; has placed on both good and soft surfaces and shown consistency without winning, but the drop back in trip after a rest could see him travel more sweetly — naturally suited to hold-up racing, he may be forced wider than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' four-year-old carries a claim for Charlie Maggs(3) and has placed three times including a third over this trip on good going; form is limited but the OR of 93 gives him a rating edge, and his preferred prominent habits may prove useful if someone has to lead by default.|

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin's five-year-old has genuine hold-up habits — placed three times in similar going — but the 84-day absence is a concern and he is boxed into a midfield map position because the field is overloaded with closers; his style fit at 0.90 tempers expectations even if he lands on a good pitch.|

runners_data.name: Louie The Legend
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's four-year-old placed on good going over 16f and has a young amateur rider in Tabitha Worsley; form is patchy (655-36) but the 30-day return is fresh enough, and a slow-run race could help a horse whose stamina has occasionally been stretched — he holds up naturally.|

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old is in strong form with four placings from five recent runs and a trainer striking at 4/21 over 14 days — the most in-form runner in the race; a natural hold-up type squeezed to midfield by the crowded rear, his OR of 87 and consistent placing suggest he could be dangerous if not trapped.|

runners_data.name: Giddyupadingdong
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old has winning form on good (1W2P) and placed third over 16f on good just recently; he is a genuine closer mapped forward on the shape due to congestion — style fit of 0.92 means he is the least penalised of the redistributed horses and a slow sprint finish could suit him well.|

runners_data.name: Rapid Mission
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's five-year-old returns from 95 days off with a limited record on today's going type and has been running over 18-24f; dropping back to 2m off a long absence is a notable query, and as a true hold-up type displaced to midfield his fitness must be assumed rather than proven.|

runners_data.name: Brenda Lady
runners_data.note: David Rees' six-year-old has minimal form — just three runs recorded — and Sean Bowen takes the ride, which provides a notable jockey upgrade; a genuine closer pushed into the midfield map slot, her limited experience on good ground (0W0P) in sim-going makes her hard to trust despite the booking.|

runners_data.name: Battle Stride
runners_data.note: Richard Armson's four-year-old is flagged for fading in finishes and returns from a lengthy 242-day absence; a sprint finish off a slow pace is probably the worst possible scenario for him, and the hold-up style crammed into midfield mapping adds further concern about his ability to land a blow here.|

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Sam England's six-year-old is also flagged as a finisher who fades and has poor recent form (006-87) with no wins or places on sim-going; the trainer has one win from four in the last 14 days, but this horse's record provides little encouragement for any race shape — the fade flag is damaging in a sprint.|

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: F Brennan's six-year-old won last time out over 20f on good going and also placed, giving her a live form line; the drop to 2m is a distance concern given her hat of staying trips, but a strong style fit of 0.92 and a winning habit means she merits respect — Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim helps at the weights.|

runners_data.name: Granny B
runners_data.note: Michael Mullineaux's six-year-old has placed four times on similar going without winning and wears headgear; Kevin Brogan takes the ride and she has consistent finishing positions in midfield without threatening — as a true closer shifted forward on the map she is unlikely to figure unless the race shapes in her favour.|

races.paceDynamic: This is an entirely hold-up dominated field at face value, yet the pace map is overloaded with horses of the same style — there is genuinely no confirmed front-runner or prominent racer prepared to take the race on from the front, meaning the field is almost certain to crawl early before bunching and producing a sprint-style finish off a slow pace. With 13 runners and none naturally drawn to lead, the race will likely see a slow-motion first circuit with jockeys eyeing each other, the pace only lifting meaningfully from the second-last or final hurdle. This shape strongly favours horses with a high cruising speed who can travel close enough to the pace without being exposed — nimble, responsive types who can quicken off a slow tempo rather than those who need a true test of stamina. Several runners including Karthala, Daring To Dream, Giddyupadingdong, Rapid Mission, Brenda Lady, Battle Stride, Littletown Lad, Lady Fortune and Granny B are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are far more closers than the shape can accommodate, and the horses most likely to naturally find a forward pitch — by default rather than design — are the higher-rated, more-experienced Character Testing, Golden Circet and Colinski, who may end up closer to the pace than their labels suggest simply through the tactical vacuum at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race degenerates into a sprint from the final hurdle, favouring the sharpest, freshest jumpers.
scenarios.body: A crawling pace means the field arrives at the last hurdle in a tight bunch, turning the race into a flat-speed contest over the run-in; horses with high cruising speed and good jump technique who can land running will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Default Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one runner or jockey takes charge by default and controls a modest gallop, stealing first run at the second-last.
scenarios.body: With no willing front-runner, a bold-jumping, front-for-default horse can dictate a comfortable, unhurried gallop and keep rivals in their own trouble; the horse who grabs a lead and jumps cleanly at every hurdle will be hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Default Pace
scenarios.trigger: If a false gallop is set before genuine hold-up horses pick off a tired early mover in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A slow-to-moderate pace suit true closers who can save ground and produce a sustained run from two out; horses with a proven late kick on good ground who avoid traffic in the bunched field will be most dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Traffic Troubles
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces significant interference, shuffling, and jumping errors that fragment the race and cause trouble in running.
scenarios.body: With 13 hold-up types crowding each other, traffic problems and jumping errors are plausible — horses with wide draws who can race away from trouble or jockeys confident enough to commit early could steal a race others find blocked.

watchPoints.text: Karthala is the one horse in this race with strong recent form (four placings from five) and an in-form trainer — watch whether Sean Quinlan can manoeuvre him into a viable position from a crowded midfield.
Battle Stride returns from 242 days off and is flagged as a fader — watch for any early signs of ring rust or jumping errors that could cause interference in a tightly packed field of 13.

Lady Fortune drops sharply in trip from 20-23f to 2m having won over staying distances — watch whether she travels with her usual fluency or comes off the bridle early as the distance becomes a question.

With no genuine front-runner in the field, watch the first two hurdles closely — whichever horse finds itself in front by default will shape the entire race, and a jockey who commits early could gain a significant tactical advantage.
Giddyupadingdong and Louie The Legend both have placing form on good ground at 16f and could be the two horses most likely to produce a sustained late run if the sprint finish develops as expected.

races.name: Bravo Benefits Celebrations Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Faye Bramley — Harry Cobden takes the ride and will be positive from the gate; good-ground similar-trip form reads 5/14 with no wins but consistent placed efforts, and an uncontested lead flatters his chance here significantly.

runners_data.name: La Pinsonniere
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's six-year-old has strong placed form at 3m-plus trips in good conditions (five placed runs from six similar-going starts) and James Bowen's patient style suits a race where tracking the pace is the key tactical advantage; the p-note suggests hood likely.

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Four wins from five over comparable trips in good-to-soft to good ground mark him as the form pick on raw figures, but pressing forward will be harder than usual in this shape — his natural front-running tendencies will be partially frustrated, tempering confidence in a smooth performance despite the Skelton yard being in excellent order (4/27 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's seven-year-old is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field, but recent form of 88-415 over shorter and weaker ground limits optimism; Beau Morgan claims 5lb and the step back to good ground is untested at this level, making this a scenario-dependent outsider.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front over this 3m trip at Uttoxeter, with La Pinsonniere and Sunray Shadow both natural prominent types — though Sunray Shadow is unlikely to secure that position naturally given the clustering of forward-going horses and has been mapped to midfield to reflect likely race reality. Sony Bill will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop given the lack of a genuine challenger for the lead, creating a rhythm that suits those who can track patiently and pounce at the right moment. Samuel Spade is the lone true hold-up runner, requiring the pace to be truly testing before his late effort can land. The field holds more prominent-minded horses than can all occupy that territory: Sony Bill is best-placed to lead, La Pinsonniere most likely to settle into a tracking role just off the pace, while Sunray Shadow will be shuffled back further than ideal. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a patient tracker who can sit just behind Sony Bill and produce a clean, measured finish — a profile that suits La Pinsonniere most naturally.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Patient Tracker Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill sets an honest but unhurried pace and a prominent tracker produces a clean round of jumping to reel him in from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill controls the tempo without being pressured, allowing La Pinsonniere to settle in a cosy tracking position before asserting from the home turn; Henderson's runner has consistent placed form at this trip and good-ground form backs this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Sustains And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill's uncontested lead gives him a rhythm that proves impossible to peg back over the final fences.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to challenge for the front, Sony Bill bowls along at his own pace and proves strong enough in a small field to hold on; Cobden's positive ride and a lightly-run race suits a horse who has shown ability at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sunray Shadow Overcomes Position
scenarios.trigger: If the Skelton-trained runner settles better than expected from his shuffled-back berth and replicates his sequence of wins at this distance.
scenarios.body: Sunray Shadow has won four of his last five over similar trips and trips in good going, and if he can travel smoothly despite his non-natural position he carries enough class to land a blow; the tongue-tie plus the Skelton yard's sharp form gives him a live outside chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final mile, turning it into a slog that brings Samuel Spade's hold-up style into play.
scenarios.body: Only a scenario where leaders capitulate badly would bring Morgan's mount into the reckoning; his recent form figures of 88-415 and a move up significantly in trip and class suggest this is a long shot rather than a live threat.

watchPoints.text: Sony Bill — if Cobden gets an uncontested lead and dictates a truly modest pace, he could prove very hard to reel in at these weights and in this small field; watch how quickly any challenger moves to close him down at the top of the straight.

Sunray Shadow — the Skelton yard are firing and this horse has serious class at the trip, but if he is checked or unbalanced early trying to find a position he doesn't naturally own, his jumping rhythm could suffer; watch his jumping in the first half mile.

La Pinsonniere — Henderson's 0/2 in the last 14 days is a soft negative, but the horse's consistent placing record in similar conditions makes him dangerous if he gets a clean run from the front turn; watch for any jumping errors given this is a novice chase context.

Samuel Spade — with only four runners, any scrimmaging or fall ahead could catapult the hold-up horse into a prominent position he wouldn't otherwise enjoy; jockey Beau Morgan on a claim is worth monitoring for positional awareness in a small field.

races.name: Sun Racing The Favourite Pullout Every Day Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Romany Brown
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Ben Case who controls this from the off; similar-going form reads 1W5P over this trip and surface, but a 254-day absence and a fall in recent form (the F in his string) raise durability questions if his jumping comes under pressure late.
runners_data.comment: A faller last time out, but that followed a win in the form and this gelding has raced over today's trip before. Rated the form pick of this six on our figures, though a 254-day absence since is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy partners this Jack Jones-trained six-year-old who has solid recent form (placed in three of last four) and a win over this exact course and distance; prominent style suits a pace-controlled race perfectly and the 27-day turnaround looks routine.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out for this gelding, who has two wins among his last four starts. He returns on a swift 27-day turnaround having raced today's trip before. Fourth of six on our figures, with more experienced form ahead of him in this line-up.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero's charge carries the tongue-strap and has winning form over 18f on good, suggesting stamina is fine; Jack Tudor takes the ride and the horse profiles well in a race where a controlled pace rewards those sitting close to the speed.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out for this gelding, who has a win among his last five starts but also a fall and a pulled-up effort further back. He has raced over today's trip before and returns off a 32-day break, third of six on our figures.

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: In-form winner of two of his last three, this Jamie Snowden five-year-old is a natural prominent racer; the field congestion up front means Gavin Sheehan will likely have to settle for a position further back than ideal, which reduces the impact of his natural racing style and discounts his chance slightly.
runners_data.comment: Won two of its last four starts, with the other two runs both thirds. A 29-day break brings it back fresh over today's trip, and that overall profile makes it our selection here.

runners_data.name: Ip Up
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood, with a course-and-distance win last time out 33 days ago for Jedd O'Keeffe and Sean Quinlan; his style requires a pace with some substance to it — he thrives if the front-runners stretch the field, but a dawdle could leave him with too much ground to make up late.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, capping a five-run sequence that never saw her finish outside the first five. Second of six on our figures and has raced over today's trip, though it took until that latest start to turn the places into a win.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy has a strong 14-day strike-rate (3/16) and Sean Bowen is a high-quality booking, but Ask A Sainte is fundamentally a front-running type who will be squeezed out of his preferred role by the busier pace picture; his chance is tempered by the likelihood he races further off the pace than suits him.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner two starts before that, so the recent form reads better than bottom-of-the-pack suggests. Still rated last of six on our figures here, and the 33-day gap since does little to change that assessment.

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's six-year-old wears a tongue-strap and most of his best form has come over shorter or softer; two miles on good at Uttoxeter stretches him on both counts, and without a win in his last five runs the hold-up profile here offers limited upside unless the race develops into a strong-pace scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Romany Brown is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, is likely to control proceedings at a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset. An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda will press forward to occupy the other prominent positions, creating a small group on or near the pace that sets a measured but not dawdling tempo over the two-mile trip. This field carries more prominent-minded horses than can realistically all get their natural berth — Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are genuine pace-lovers who are both mapped to midfield because Romany Brown, An Bradan Feasa, and King Ulanda are likely to dominate the front ranks, forcing them to settle further back than ideal. A single, uncontested front-runner dictating a controlled pace over two miles on good ground at Uttoxeter strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can track close to the action and pounce in the straight, rather than those needing a strong gallop to produce a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Romany Brown Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Romany Brown leads unchallenged throughout and the tempo remains controlled, setting up a tactical finish.
scenarios.body: Romany Brown exploits a clear lead to dictate every stride, and those tracking closest — An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda — find themselves ideally placed to challenge approaching the last; a steady pace means the race is decided by class and jumping rather than stamina. Prominent, close-tracking horses benefit most as the lack of pressure keeps the race within reach of those ridden handily.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach or Ask A Sainte push forward and force a stronger gallop, changing the race tempo significantly.
scenarios.body: A contested pace from around halfway stretches the field and increases the premium on jumping cleanly and sustaining effort; horses with proven stamina and a higher cruising speed benefit most. Ip Up, as a genuine hold-up type with a recent win over the course and distance, comes into play if the race develops into more of a genuine test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and the leaders tie up, leaving late energy at a premium.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race that suddenly quickens in the final two furlongs can see prominent horses flounder if they have expended energy chasing a false tempo earlier; genuine hold-up runners benefit if they have been kept fresh. Ip Up and St Just In Time carry profiles that could take advantage of a late surge, though neither is a true sit-and-sprint type.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Disrupt Order
scenarios.trigger: If significant jumping mistakes reshuffle the field or remove key protagonists from contention.
scenarios.body: Romany Brown's recent form string includes a fall, and any error at a critical hurdle could transform the race shape entirely; fluent jumpers in behind would inherit a clear positional advantage. King Ulanda, who has the experience to capitalise on a vacuum at the front, and An Bradan Feasa would be immediate beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Romany Brown's fall (F) in recent form combined with a 254-day layoff means any jumping error or early pressure could instantly reshape this race — watch him at the early hurdles.

Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are both natural front-runners who cannot all get their preferred position — monitor the first two furlongs to see whether either pushes forward regardless, which would significantly alter the pace scenario.

Ip Up's hold-up style means he requires at least a moderate gallop to close into; if the pace is truly sedate behind Romany Brown, watch whether Sean Quinlan elects to alter his tactics and push closer than usual.

King Ulanda's tongue-strap is a first-time headgear flag worth watching at the start and in the early stages — if it has a settling effect, it could allow Jack Tudor to dictate exactly where in the race he commits.

races.name: Alfie Flatt 18th Birthday Celebration Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Theonlywayiswessex
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field, Alan King's eight-year-old has solid Good-ground form (2W8P in similar conditions) and arrives 42 days fresh; with no rival expected to seriously dispute the lead, its ability to control tempo and jump cleanly from the front is the central race factor, though the [STYLE_FIT] tag flags it is technically racing slightly out of its most comfortable role and finishing positions can be vulnerable if the race develops into a proper jumping test.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, capping a string of frames in its last five starts and it has raced over today's trip before. Rated only fifth of five in this small field, though, with more improved efforts above it on our figures.

runners_data.name: Pep Talking
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's eight-year-old boasts the best relevant form figures here — five wins and ten places in Good conditions — and has posted three consecutive runner-up finishes showing it is consistent and course-fit; naturally prominent, it should slot cleanly into second place behind the sole front-runner, giving Gavin Sheehan a straightforward sit with a jumping advantage if the race develops as anticipated.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and rarely far away, with a win three starts back and past starts over today's trip. Third of five on our figures, though a pulled-up effort further back in the sequence is the blot to note.

runners_data.name: Ukantango
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's nine-year-old is the genuine hold-up horse in this field, with Sean Bowen likely to settle last or second-last and rely on the leaders setting enough of a gallop to get into the race late; the tongue-strap and cheekpieces are noted headgear angles, but the uncontested early pace of Theonlywayiswessex may not be brisk enough over 2m4f to suit a closer, making Ukantango dependent on circumstances rather than race shape.
runners_data.comment: A winner in two of its last five starts, including three starts back, and sits top of this five on our figures. Below-par when ninth last time out, though, with the 54-day layoff since raising a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Le Gentleman
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor's lightly-raced five-year-old has strong raw form — two wins and two places in four Good-ground runs — but is a true prominent racer whose natural position is near the front; with Theonlywayiswessex dominating the pace and Pep Talking also wanting to be handy, this horse is pushed back into a midfield slot that doesn't suit its instincts, and the [STYLE_FIT] discount applies here in a field where it simply cannot get the position it needs.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out for this gelding. A winner earlier in this sequence, he returns fresh off a rapid 19-day turnaround having raced this trip before. That fitness edge and a progressive profile make him our pick, without the very top figure on our book.

runners_data.name: My Friend Sean
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's seven-year-old has struggled for form recently (form string: 6636-5) and is another horse who wants to race prominently but cannot in this crowded pace scenario; Stan Sheppard will find it hard to engineer a good early position with two other front-runners ahead of him, and the horse's best Good-ground figures (9/15 in similar conditions) suggest it is not reliable enough to overcome the tactical disadvantage of racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, though a third-placed effort in that sequence hints at more, and our figures rate it well above its official mark. Second of five here, despite a form line dotted with three sixth-placed runs.

races.paceDynamic: Theonlywayiswessex is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, will be allowed to roll along at a controlled, self-chosen tempo over 2m4f at Uttoxeter. Pep Talking and Le Gentleman are both naturally prominent types, but with three horses wanting to race up with the pace in a field of five, Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are unlikely to secure their preferred berths and will be shuffled back from their natural position. That compressed pace picture means Theonlywayiswessex can dictate every yard, keep it honest without being pressured, and essentially set the terms for the finish. This shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can sit just behind the leader in a good rhythm and produce a clean jumping round — Pep Talking, who is a genuine hold-near-the-pace type with excellent form in Good conditions, is ideally placed to benefit, while hold-up operators like Ukantango will need the early pace to be generous enough to create a target late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Theonlywayiswessex dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field settles into a neat single-file procession.
scenarios.body: Theonlywayiswessex controls the tempo from the front and jumps efficiently, making the race a thorough test of stamina at a fair but not frenetic pace; a horse tracking in second or third with clean jumping can challenge from two out without needing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Pep Talking travels smoothly in second throughout and pounces on Theonlywayiswessex approaching the last two fences.
scenarios.body: Pep Talking's strong Good-ground form and recent second-place efforts at this trip suggest it has the class and fitness to overhaul the leader when asked; the uncontested early pace means Pep Talking won't be asked a question until the business end, exactly suiting its profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to string out the field and Ukantango closes powerfully from off the pace in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Ukantango has won off a hold-up style before and Sean Bowen will be patient, but the steady tempo set by an uncontested Theonlywayiswessex may not generate enough early fractions to bring a closer into play; it needs something to go wrong up front and the race to be run at a genuinely searching gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Front
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses scramble for position early or jumping errors reshuffle the order, breaking up Theonlywayiswessex's lead.
scenarios.body: In a small field where Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are squeezed out of their natural prominence, a stumble or early contest for position could unsettle the pace picture and hand an unlikely winner the initiative; with only five runners this is low-probability but not impossible.

watchPoints.text: Watch Theonlywayiswessex's jumping — as the lone pace-setter over fences, any blunder at a fence could immediately open the door to Pep Talking or even gift Le Gentleman a position it otherwise cannot secure.

Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean both want to be prominent and with Pep Talking also pressing forward, monitor the first three fences for a scrappy battle for position that could disrupt the expected settled order.

Ukantango's chance hinges almost entirely on whether Theonlywayiswessex sets a genuinely strong early gallop — if the pace is pedestrian, Sean Bowen's hold-up tactics will leave this horse with too much ground to make up from the second-last fence.

Pep Talking is fitted with headgear (hg:p) — watch whether it travels more positively than in recent outings, as Gavin Sheehan's ability to get the best from the horse in the early stages will define whether it can get first run on Theonlywayiswessex at the second-last.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Cello
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with solid good-ground credentials, but at 17 days since last run and over a trip stretching to 2m7½f, will need the pace to lift to get competitive; trainer Harry Fry has only 1 runner in the past 14 days for 0 wins.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out in a campaign that's brought a third, a fifth and a sixth plus one fall, without a win. A rapid 17-day turnaround gives a fitness edge, and that overall profile makes it our selection despite lacking the very best figure.

runners_data.name: Kayla's Friend
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical context for this entire race; rated OR 97 and drawn on recent winning form, but her STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 flags she may not be entirely at ease in her designated role if the race shape shifts around her.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, but that followed modest efforts including a sixth and one unplaced run earlier in the sequence. Only eighth of ten on our figures and below its official mark too, which points to a stiff task today.

runners_data.name: Camshaft
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the mount on this lightly-weighted five-year-old whose sole win in similar going came over 23f at Goodwood — the trip suits, and his naturally prominent style means he will be right in the mix throughout; 53 days between runs is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: The most eye-catching form here on paper - two wins in a row, its last two starts - and past starts over today's trip too. A 53-day absence since is the obvious concern, though, in a race that features fresher rivals.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with four consecutive fourth-place finishes on good ground, suggesting a reliable but limited profile; Jack Quinlan keeps the ride and the consistent placing record means she is rarely far away late, though she has yet to convert any chance at OR 96.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but consistent, no worse than fourth in any of its last five starts and better than that twice. Top of this ten on our figures, rated above its official mark, though turning places into a win remains the question.

runners_data.name: Grey Gamble
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes tactical placement uncertain; Emma Lavelle's runner has placed twice in recent good-ground outings but the trainer's T14 record of 0/3 and no wins over similar going suggests this is a difficult race to anchor her in.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but rarely too far away, fourth last time out having also raced over today's trip before. Third of ten on our figures, rated above its official mark, though an eighth-placed effort in the sequence shows there's inconsistency to watch.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran with three placed efforts in her last five good-ground starts; Joshua Thompson claims 5lb and the combination of age and that inexperienced pilot in a race of this complexity is a real concern, though her course experience is a marginal plus.
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form on the face of it, the best of it a fourth-placed effort earlier in the sequence, but rated well above its official mark. Fourth of ten on our figures nonetheless, though the placings have drifted the wrong way since, down to eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Faerie Cutlass
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent in style but has not won in 15 similar-going starts, and the headgear record (tongue-tie, pads) suggests a horse that needs everything to go right; 53 days off the track for a yard with 0/0 in the last fortnight makes freshness a minor query.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in a modest recent sequence that includes an unseated effort, though the fourth-placed run in there is the pick of it. Seventh of ten on our figures, though still rated above its official mark, with the 53-day gap since adding to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Two wins and five placings over 24f on good ground give her the clearest stamina credentials in this field; Sara Ender's T14 record of 1/3 is modest but the horse's form figures over distance on this surface are the most compelling of any hold-up runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and only fair form generally, though there's a win four starts back to note and past starts over today's trip. Ninth of ten on our figures here, making it one of the outsiders in this field on assessment.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: A four-year-old whose form has tightened dramatically to consecutive second and third finishes over 23-24f on good ground — Megan Bevan's 7lb claim is a significant weight advantage, and the blinkers headgear suggests the yard is trying to sharpen her focus; open-to-improvement profile.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and runner-up two starts before that, an improving pair of efforts after finishing down the field previously. Sixth of ten on our figures, rated above its official mark, though it's yet to turn those placings into a win.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose position on the map reflects the congested rear of the field rather than his true role — Jack Tudor is a high-quality pilot, but the OR 75 and a sequence of moderate efforts at shorter trips over good ground make improvement here a tough ask; Christian Williams's T14 reads 0/6.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last four starts, no better than fifth and pulled up once in the mix. Bottom of ten on our figures and below its official mark too, with only a quick 12-day turnaround in its favour.

races.paceDynamic: Kayla's Friend is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her, should slot into an uncontested lead and dictate a measured, manageable gallop over this 2m7½f trip. Camshaft and Faerie Cutlass are both naturally prominent types who will seek to sit close to the pace, creating a compact lead group but unlikely to apply serious pressure to Kayla's Friend unless the jockey on Camshaft — Jonjo O'Neill Jr. — elects to press. Behind them, Hello Cello, Blackwater Lilly, and Theirshegoes will track from further back, with Grey Gamble and Athena's Dream's roles undefined given their unclassified styles. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the map can neatly place — Global Hideaway is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield, and Belladinotte may also find herself further back than ideal. This race shape — a controlled, single-pacemaker tempo over a long trip — strongly favours prominent horses who can settle close to the frugal gallop and pounce early in the straight, rather than late closers who will need a fast pace to generate momentum from off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend sets an unchallenged, measured pace and the prominent horses track comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Kayla's Friend dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, with Camshaft and Faerie Cutlass sitting close enough to pounce before the race develops into a true stamina test; the winner comes from the front two or three in the straight with first run. This suits horses who can race prominently without being buried in traffic, and Camshaft's recent winning form on good ground over this trip marks him as the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Steadies, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend sets an especially slow early tempo, compressing the field and inviting a late sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slowly-run race brings the hold-up horses back into contention as the pace quickens sharply off the home turn, negating the advantage of those who tracked close. Hello Cello and Blackwater Lilly, both consistent hold-up performers on good ground, would benefit from a flat-out dash to the line on this longer trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft or Faerie Cutlass elects to press Kayla's Friend from early on, injecting real gallop into proceedings.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested pace over 2m7½f turns the race into a stamina grind, burning off prominent horses who pushed forward without reserves; those who settled quietly in midfield and have stamina in their profile will stay on best. Belladinotte, who has strong form over 24f on good ground and has won at the trip, and Hello Cello, proven over marathon distances, are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down tactically — interference, falls, or a dramatic change of pace mid-race — and the field is reordered.
scenarios.body: A fragmented race over hurdles over this distance can produce a shock result, with a horse like Athena's Dream — progressive form, recent top-two finishes, and low weight — catching the eye as an each-way player in disrupted conditions. Theirshegoes's course and distance experience could also prove relevant if the front rank capitulates late.

watchPoints.text: Camshaft is the primary danger in this race shape — his two wins both came on good ground over the distance range, he sits right behind the pace with a top jockey, and 53 days since last run could mean a fresh, well-placed run if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. gives him a positive ride.

Monitor how Kayla's Friend is ridden in the opening mile — if Sean Bowen allows her to loaf at a crawl, the field will compress and the advantage of her front-running role is eliminated, dramatically changing which scenario plays out.

Belladinotte's trainer T14 record of 1/3 and recent form of 41-046 suggest inconsistency, but her stamina credentials over exactly this distance on good ground mean she must not be ignored if the pace increases and turns it into a true test.

Athena's Dream carries only 147lbs with a 7lb claimer and has finished second and third in her last two starts over the distance range — if the race develops into a prolonged gallop, her lighter weight and improving profile make her a live outsider to place.

Global Hideaway's redistribution to midfield disguises the fact he is a true hold-up type — watch whether Jack Tudor is able to find his natural position at the rear, and if not, his chance is further compromised by having to race out of role.
